semantics: Every label the agentic-layer generator emits is listed here and scored. Gold that fails its own checksum (the invalid twins) stays scored, exactly as in the Kiji validator gold census; the per-label validity split is reported beside it and never replaces it. Layer A adjacent-address gold uses synthetic private-network host endpoints associated with a user's device. Documentation, loopback and link-local ranges are benign and scored as Layer D lookalikes instead. Layer D documents carry no gold, so every byte predicted there is a false positive. Layer R decoys (words spelled like or containing a name part, digit runs shared with a repeated identifier) are not gold either, so a byte predicted over one is a false positive; every repeat of a real value is gold. An unlisted label fails closed, and so does a ruling on a label the generator no longer emits.
